newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - July 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - July 7.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY
- Anti-Japan Memorial Hall receives more than 130,000 Japanese tourists.
- A million college and high school students to spend summer vacation in the countryside to provide cultural, technological and medical aid.
- The first group of Hong Kong tourists to Beijing since July 1 go sight-seeing and attend celebrations for the return of Hong Kong.
XINHUA DAILY TELEGRAPH
- More than 2,000 Chinese enterprises chosen for experiments with modern management systems produce 42 billion yuan profits in 1996, more than the national average.
- An editorial lashes out at Japanese who deny the war of aggression against China 1937-1945.
CHINA DAILY
- Afforestation is being accelerated to ease acute fuel shortages in rural areas and help conserve dwindling forests.
- Life expectancy reaches 76 in Shanghai
- Sino-Indian Joint Business Council starts meeting in Beijing
CHINA SECURITIES
- State firms in pilot scheme to be restructured into share-holding companies show improvement.
INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS DAILY
- China cement exports hit 11.8 million tonnes in 1996.
ECONOMIC DAILY
- China needs to find jobs for 160-180 million people in 1996-2000.
- China completes installation of temporary lock for the Three Gorges Dam on the Yangtze River.
- China Jialing Industry Co and Zhejiang-based Jili Group to form Zhejiang Jialing Motorcycle Co.
FUTURES HERALD
- China net grain imports estimated at 10 billion kg in 1996.
- Average national price of wheat seen at 1,516 yuan per tonne in June, down 5.72 percent from May.
FINANCIAL NEWS
- Vice-Minister of State Planning Commission Ma Kai says macro-controls have helped bring down inflation.
- China Construction Bank boosts checks on funds used for resettlement of population from Three Gorges Dam area.
- Industrial and Commercial Bank of China signs agreement with Hexun Co to collect Internet fees nationwide.
- Signed article calls for unified supervision system for stock markets and greater role for China Securities Regulatory Commission
MARKET DAILY
- China's annual movie goers fall to eight billion in 1996, from 29.3 billion in 1984.
- Henan province cuts prices of oil products to maintain sales.
- Heavy oil prices soar in Hunan because of short supply.
